XENERGY, Inc. (1998). United States Industrial Electric Motor Systems Market Opportunities Assessment. Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Industrial Technologies, and Oak Ridge National Laboratory (Lockheed Martin Energy Research). Burlington, MA, December 1998; reprinted by DOE EERE Office of Industrial Technologies (BestPractices), December 2002, with minor corrections to the appendices. No report number or DOI printed.

Corporate author XENERGY Inc. (title page); no individual authors, so the id stays xenergy_1998_001. Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 9 in Section 1 up to p.51, printed + 8 from p.53; appendices numbered A-/B-/C-/D-). Targeted pass (386 pp): Executive Summary and Sections 1-2. Main file: nominal full-load efficiencies by 19 hp ranges for three motor levels (MotorMaster+ default of standard motors in use, EPAct minimum, CEE premium; Table 2-10) and lifetime derived as 40,000 mean lifetime operating hours / mean annual hours by hp class (Table 2-11). No per-measure or per-motor costs are printed in Sections 1-2 (only the 11-17 billion USD aggregate investment and the 3-year payback criterion), so no capex. Operating hours are in _other-values (no mean load factor printed, only the part-load distribution, so no capacity factor). _measures: savings fractions and applicability for pump, compressed air and fan measures (Tables 2-4, 2-6, 2-8), downsizing (Table 2-9), efficient-replacement population savings (Table 2-15), rewinds, Table 2-1 ranges and the 13 Showcase projects (Table E-3). Not extracted: Appendix A industry profiles and case studies (paybacks only), Appendix B standard tables by SIC, Appendices C-D (methods, stock model), Section 3 purchase practices.

(4) Table 2-10 efficiencies are for 1800 rpm motors only. (5) The 40,000 h lifetime is time to failure; most large failed motors are rewound (Table 2-11).
